guide.summary: Sandbox testing only (self-serve, wait none); Production REST Pay app for merchants (app review, wait unknown, reported up to about 4 months).
guide.verdict: Sandbox-only testing needs no approval; a production app needs developer account approval plus app review, with no documented timeline and one reported 4-month wait.

composio.note: Clover is in Composio's bring-your-own-OAuth-app list. Create the auth config with your own Clover app credentials.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio provides no managed OAuth app for Clover, so you must register your own Clover app and supply its client ID and secret to Composio.
reasons: No Composio-managed app exists for Clover
Dedicated quota instead of shared managed quota
Consent screen shows your brand, not Composio's

scenarios.label: Sandbox testing only
scenarios.when_this_applies: You only build and test in the Clover sandbox and no outside merchants connect.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: Account approval is not needed for sandbox-only use (c2).

scenarios.approval: No developer account approval is needed for sandbox-only use.

scenarios.label: Production REST Pay app for merchants
scenarios.when_this_applies: You take your app live so outside Clover merchants authorize it through OAuth, for example an agent acting for merchants.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count and documents needed, not measured

waiting.estimate: Unknown, reported up to about 4 months
waiting.basis: Official FAQ gives no timeline (c19); one developer reported about 4 months pending (c17).

scenarios.approval: Clover must approve your production developer account first, then the app goes through approval. Later changes to the approved app are reviewed again.

modifiers.note: Owner role and approved production developer account needed.

extras: Owner role and approved production developer account needed.

prerequisites.title: Approved production developer account
prerequisites.detail: Clover must verify and approve it before app approval starts; it is not needed for sandbox-only use.

prerequisites.title: Owner role
prerequisites.detail: Only an owner can accept the Clover Developer Agreement and edit account settings.

prerequisites.title: Identity and business documents
prerequisites.detail: Needs date of birth, home address proof, passport or driver's license, and for companies a 9-character EIN/Tax ID plus proof of business address.

steps.title: Create global developer account and sandbox app
steps.detail: Create a global developer account, then create and test the app on the sandbox.

steps.title: Submit production developer account for approval
steps.detail: In the production Developer Dashboard go to Developer Settings > Info, fill each section, and click Verify Your Account. Choose Individual or Business.

steps.title: Answer document requests within 10 business days
steps.detail: If Clover emails for more documents, upload them to the secure Clover Box, not by email.

steps.title: Configure the production app
steps.detail: Draft the app settings: REST Pay permissions, Site URL, Default OAuth Response set to Code, and the OAuth URL. Do not leave the app on sandbox settings or broken redirect links.

steps.title: Wait for Clover app approval
steps.detail: No official timeline exists; contact Developer Relations if it runs long.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your Clover client credentials, using the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

traps.title: After a 429 response, the app must pause one
traps.detail: After a 429 response, the app must pause one second before making another API request, and if 429s continue it must increase the wait exponentially.

traps.title: No review timeline and reported long waits
traps.detail: Clover gives no fixed timeline, and one developer reported about 4 months pending with a reported backlog. Plan a launch with slack.

traps.title: Sandbox settings left in code
traps.detail: Clover says common failures are leaving the code on Sandbox instead of Production and broken redirect links.

traps.title: Document deadline
traps.detail: Requested documents must arrive within 10 business days or the application may be rejected.

traps.title: Revisions are reviewed again
traps.detail: Changes to permissions, site URL, listing icon and legal links on an approved app need DevRel review.

blockers.what_it_means: The app exceeded Clover's rate limits, 16 new requests per second per token.
blockers.what_to_do: Pause one second, then back off exponentially if 429s continue.
blockers.agent_can_help: Add retry with backoff to the client.

blockers.symptom: Application rejected or stalled in review
blockers.what_it_means: Functionality, legal and privacy, or listing problems are common causes.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix the cited issues, resubmit, and contact Developer Relations if it stalls.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check redirect links and prepare listing content.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Create a production developer account as described in Developer account approval .
evidence.answer: Creating a production Clover app requires a production developer account, which must be approved first (per the linked Developer account approval page).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: External POS apps using the REST Pay API are not available on the public Clover App market, but your Clover apps are visible to merchants using your integrated POS.
evidence.answer: For external POS apps using the REST Pay API, the app is not listed on the public Clover App market; it is visible to merchants using the developer's integrated POS.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: To complete a payment on the Clover device, you must authorize your app to read merchant data from a Clover device.
evidence.answer: For card-present transactions, the app must request READ permission for Merchant, with a reason text entered in the reason field.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: In the reason field, enter Required to connect POS app to Clover device using REST Pay API .
evidence.answer: For card-present transactions, the reason entered for the Merchant READ permission is 'Required to connect POS app to Clover device using REST Pay API'.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If your app lets merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens for card-not-present (CNP) transactions, you must also configure your app for the Ecommerce API.
evidence.answer: Card-not-present support is optional and applies only if the app lets merchants create and use ECOMM_COMPAT card tokens; then the app must also be configured for the Ecommerce API.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: In the Ecommerce section, select the Enable online payments checkbox.
evidence.answer: For card-not-present transactions, the developer selects the Enable online payments checkbox in the Ecommerce section of Requested Permissions.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In the Site URL field, enter the link (URL) of the home page of your web app.
evidence.answer: The Site URL is set to the link (URL) of the home page of the developer's web app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Optionally, if you are integrating with Cloud Pay Display, enter a domain link (URL) in the CORS Domain field.
evidence.answer: An optional CORS Domain URL is entered only when integrating with Cloud Pay Display.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: When you set a CORS domain URL, your web app can make calls to the Clover REST API without requiring an intermediate app server.
evidence.answer: A CORS domain URL lets the web app call the Clover REST API without an intermediate app server.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Log in to Developer Dashboard .
evidence.answer: To create the app, log in to the Developer Dashboard, click Create App, enter an app name, and select the countries where the app is available for Clover merchants.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Select one or more countries where you want to make your app available for Clover merchants.
evidence.answer: Select one or more countries where the app will be available to Clover merchants when creating the app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Click Create . The App name - App Settings page appears.
evidence.answer: Clicking Create in the Create App window opens the app's App Settings page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: For - Is this app an integration of an existing point of sale? option - select Yes .
evidence.answer: For a semi-integrated POS app, set App Type by selecting REST Clients > Web and answering Yes to whether the app is an integration of an existing point of sale.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The App Settings—App Type section displays a Remote App ID (RAID) that uniquely identifies your semi-integrated app.
evidence.answer: After saving the app type, the App Settings page shows a Remote App ID (RAID) that uniquely identifies the semi-integrated app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: In the Default OAuth Response field, select Code .
evidence.answer: Under Default OAuth Response, the developer selects Code, which yields an authorization code when a merchant authorizes via OAuth 2.0.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Your app needs OAuth tokens to authenticate API calls.
evidence.answer: The app needs OAuth tokens to authenticate API calls, so a URL for the OAuth flow must be configured in REST Configuration.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: When your merchant is authorized through OAuth 2.0, you receive an authorization code.
evidence.answer: When a merchant is authorized through OAuth 2.0, the app receives an authorization code, which is required to request an API token for the app's permissions.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The app lets you configure merchant permissions and URLs needed to retrieve OAuth tokens.
evidence.answer: Configuration of the app's merchant permissions and the URLs needed to retrieve OAuth tokens is done on the created app.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: In the app revisions review and approval process, the Clover Developer Relations (DevRel) team thoroughly reviews the submitted changes and approves or rejects the request.
evidence.answer: Clover DevRel reviews the submitted changes and approves or rejects them. This applies to revisions to approved or published apps.

evidence.answer: Clover DevRel reviews app icon changes on the Market Listing (for revisions to approved or published apps).

evidence.answer: Clover DevRel reviews requested app permission changes on the App Settings (for revisions to approved or published apps).

evidence.question: G3

The quotes support account approval and app submission, but do not say that merchants can install only after passing review.
The quotes say Clover verifies individual and corporate information. They do not mention checks on data need, a working demo, or the listing.
